posts.author: ARIOSODEV
posts.body:
Random idea that came to my head as I woke up this morning.
(Roughly a few minutes ago.)
So, I'm assuming you guys are familiar with the concept of game jams, so I'll brush over explaining that. But I had this idea where, what if there was a sort of similar competition, but instead of creating an entire game, you're tasked with creating a set of UIs surrounding a theme? Like, the battle HUD, menus, messages, etc.
I mean this as in actually coding it into a blank project too, not just creating concepts in a drawing application.
Then again, not sure if there are people out there that're really
that
enthusiastic about UI design, lol.
Silly idea that came to my head, what do you guys think?

posts.author: rainytei
posts.body:
Wait, no! I think it's a really cool idea!! I mean, isn't one of the main points of game jams to encourage creativity and innovation in the community? And UI is actually a huge part of game development that is super overlooked in the rpg maker community. I mean, over in MV world, I can't count how many times I've seen just the basic menus or, as like one of the only alternatives, Yanfly stuff.
It wouldn't be for everyone, as UI can get kinda complicated, but in general game jams don't strike everyone's fancy. I've never felt the urge to participate in a game jam, but I'd be all over this.

posts.author: Zia_
posts.body:
I wouldn't participate (in no kind of Jam or Contest, as I dedicate all my time in my project), but I also think, this is a very good idea.
As a source of inspiration it could spark new designs or even game or feature ideas. As you don't have to think about making game mechanic part work aswell, you could put in all the stuff you dream of.
It can also inspire the way of arranging elements, make cryptic game elements intuitive and reduce the amount of unnecessary information to make it readable. And the way of animating all the stuff might also kickstart something.
Not sure, how many people would participate, but I would be interested in the results.
PS: I just wouldn't focus too much about the "coding" stuff. I don't care how the UI is presented. A video might be even better to showcase every function. As some people are great in graphics but couldn't turn it into a Plugin or something.

posts.author: RCXGaming
posts.body:
fop said:
And, I mean, I don't think regular game jams are worth it personally--why put in work to make what's usually a very short game?
Click to expand...
I just had to say something to this.
It's to build your skills. To test the waters for future mechanics so you see how they function in a more contained context. To see how your writing goes over with an audience without having to spend an inordinate amount of time with build-up.
The point of game jams isn't to make a real game since you'd be lucky to finish in the time allotted, but to test how your work ethic functions under pressure.
It also helps build your portfolio so people like artists/musicians/coders can see what you're capable of.
---
As for the actual topic of the thread, a UI competition could be neat but part of the issue is that it'd require a lot of custom artwork or coding to really stand out, which doesn't seem like it'd attract a lot of people to participate.
That, and the best UI designs aren't made in a vacuum, they need an underlying game to give them context.

posts.author: TRIDIUM
posts.body:
In addition to what RCX said, tons of authors write short stories, filmmakers make short films, mangaka's write one shots. Sometimes, all you need is 15 minutes or so to tell a story.
Also they're fun.
As for a UI jam, while I'm personally not a huge fan of making UI's myself, I do like the idea of focusing in on a specific element of game design, rather than a whole game for a jam.

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
Just to jump in with two thoughts.
#1
I learned a LOT by participating in my first game jam. And it motivated me to get back into using MZ after I took a break for a few months. I think there is a lot of value in doing a short project from start to finish and game jams can help facilitate that. I think they can be a very good learning experience. With that said, while I don't regret participating and the experience was very valuable, I'm not rushing back to participate in another one unless I am really inspired by the topic.
#2
I wouldn't be interested in participating in a UI game jam, but I would actually love to see a thread dedicated to showing UIs that have been developed along with a short explanation of what was used. Like if it was Evented or if plugins were used. And if applicable, what plugin(s) and approximately how long it took. I would love to see what other people have done for UIs and how they did it.
